# Practice Runtime architecture

`ms-go-practice-runtime` is the owner of a learner's Practice V2 execution after selecting a published Catalog revision. It stores TaskInstances, Submissions, ValidationRuns, lifecycle and review receipts, and the outbox event that requests Student evidence application. It does not own a V2 `Attempt` entity.

## Ownership boundaries

| Service | Owns | Practice Runtime interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pet Project Orchestrator / Catalog | Published revision and private evaluation context | Supplies an immutable exact-revision envelope and digest |
| Student | LearningAction, evidence, mastery, and path state | Reserves and opens an action; accepts final evidence idempotently |
| Learning Planner | Canonical route and materialized learning content | Returns an immutable route receipt |
| Sandbox | Runtime workspace, file contents, pinned generations, write fences | Creates or resumes a stable workspace; freezes and serves exact snapshots |
| Validation Orchestrator | Validation execution and stage semantics | Evaluates a typed request against an exact pinned snapshot |
| Teacher Agent | Assistance and explanatory output | Receives safe projections and appends assistance; cannot decide results |
| Human mentor | Human review decision | Approves or requests changes through the authorized Runtime command |

## Durable lifecycle

Start persists a resumable receipt with the exact revision projection before provisioning external resources. Replays use that frozen projection, not the Catalog's current revision. A TaskInstance is ready only when Student, Planner, Sandbox, and Runtime receipts agree on the exact identities and digests.

Submit stores a scoped idempotency intent before asking Sandbox to freeze the workspace. The returned pin identifies one immutable generation and digest. Runtime commits the Submission, first ValidationRun, and `VALIDATING` TaskInstance state together. Retries reuse that snapshot and validation contract; technical evaluation failures are `ERROR`, separate from learner `FAIL`.

Final completion requires all required milestones, a passing final Submission, any required human approval, and acknowledgement of the Sandbox permanent write lock. The completion transaction also inserts one final Student evidence event into the outbox. Delivery may retry, using the final Submission ID as `evidence_id`, without changing the Practice result.

## Package boundaries

The domain defines lifecycle values and invariants. Application ports describe semantic capabilities; use cases coordinate transactions and side effects. HTTP and provider adapters map external DTOs at boundaries. PostgreSQL repositories persist local state and receipts. The Go composition root wires the listener, database, repositories, and adapters. See `.ai/architecture.yaml` for the package map.

## Accepted Hybrid Replanning protection (Problem #4)

The authoritative [Hybrid Mastery → Replanning decision](https://github.com/bemulima/ms-go-learning-planner/blob/main/docs/hybrid-mastery-replanning.md) keeps Practice
execution here and learner Evidence/Mastery/Path state in Student. Runtime results
may inform Planner evaluation through Student; they never directly rewrite Path.
Ordinary replan protects the ACTIVE item, existing TaskInstance, frozen revision,
workspace binding, and learner/item association.

Pause/resume of an existing TaskInstance is optional; ordinary replan never requires
it. Critical remediation can interrupt ACTIVE Practice only with explicit student
intent and supported safe checkpoint/hold/resume, preserving the same TaskInstance
and return association. Without this capability, ACTIVE Practice is not interrupted
for remediation; remediation waits for the ordinary safe boundary. Capability
absence does not block Hybrid Replanning. This closure implements no pause/resume
and does not extend the frozen V2 contract.

The Activity/Revision owner confirms INVALID content, such as broken requirements
or invalid tests. Runtime confirms IMPOSSIBLE execution of otherwise valid activity
in its current context, such as unavailable provisioning, capability, environment,
or resources. For Practice, Runtime authority is `ms-go-practice-runtime`. Planner
decides the planning consequence; Student applies authoritative learner/Path state.
Neither fact permits orphaning or silently cancelling the TaskInstance.
Path mutation atomicity does not imply a cross-service Runtime transaction. This
documentation changes no lifecycle, completion, provider wire contract, or
Problem #1/#3 semantics.

## Authoritative Next Best Action (Problem #5)

Student owns the learner-wide `NextActionResolver`; Planner continues to own
strategic routes. Runtime supplies the additive read-only
[Student execution projection](../contracts/student-execution-projection-v1.md).
It normalizes internal execution states into bounded status, permitted actions,
an exact required milestone/submission target, reason, identity and snapshot
provenance. Student consumes these facts without duplicating this state machine.
Teacher/UI consume Student's decision. Student intent then invokes the existing
owner's command, which validates current invariants again. The projection never
executes commands or updates Student state, and preserves frozen V2 semantics.
